root_cause.text: The function wl1271_tx_allocate() returns -EAGAIN (which the caller interprets as a transient aggregation-buffer-full condition) when pskb_expand_head() fails due to insufficient memory, causing wlcore_tx_work_locked() to retry the same skb in an infinite loop and result in a CPU soft lockup.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that after commit e75665dd0968, wl1271_tx_allocate() and wl1271_prepare_tx_frame() return -EAGAIN on pskb_expand_head() failure. In wlcore_tx_work_locked(), -EAGAIN is misinterpreted as "aggregation buffer being full", leading to immediate retry of the same skb. Because the failure is actually a memory allocation error (non-transient), the retry never succeeds, causing an infinite loop. The patch fixes this by returning -ENOMEM instead, which causes the packet to be dropped and the loop to terminate.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error code in wl1271_tx_allocate to return -ENOMEM (instead of -EAGAIN) when pskb_expand_head fails due to memory shortage.
intent_record.what: In the function wl1271_tx_allocate, when pskb_expand_head fails, the return value is changed from -EAGAIN to -ENOMEM.
intent_record.how: This change alters the error code returned to callers when pskb_expand_head fails, indicating memory allocation failure instead of a retryable condition.

grouping_result.intent: Fix error code in wl1271_tx_allocate to return -ENOMEM (instead of -EAGAIN) when pskb_expand_head fails due to memory shortage.

relevance_review.reason: The group changes the error return code from -EAGAIN to -ENOMEM when pskb_expand_head fails, directly preventing the infinite retry loop that caused the CPU soft lockup, which is the core vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: Returning -EAGAIN when pskb_expand_head fails due to insufficient memory is misinterpreted by the caller as a transient aggregation-buffer-full condition, causing infinite retry and CPU soft lockup.

vuln_statements.explanation: When pskb_expand_head() fails due to insufficient memory, wl1271_tx_allocate() returns -EAGAIN, which the caller (wlcore_tx_work_locked) interprets as a transient aggregation-buffer-full condition. This causes the same skb to be retried indefinitely, leading to a CPU soft lockup. The correct error code should be -ENOMEM to indicate a permanent memory allocation failure, so the caller will properly discard the skb and stop retrying.
